column1: # THE skill-routing table — the single source of truth for every routing surface.
# Routing a skill used to take six coordinated edits (README's two tables, the runbook row,
# init-project.sh's CLAUDE.local.md heredoc, gate-check.sh's stage map, the agent templates)
# plus a seventh copy inside every project's CLAUDE.local.md that no script could update.
# Measured on 2026-08-18, before this file existed: 17 of 43 skills were routed by NOTHING a
# project agent reads; facts-lock.sh reached 1 of 6 wired projects; agent-roles.md and
# source-triage.md reached 1 each. Every skill added since had silently become the eighteenth.
# Edit THIS file, then run:  bin/render-routing.sh
# CI / gate:                 bin/render-routing.sh --check   (exit 2 == a surface has drifted)
# Format: TAB-separated, seven columns. Blank lines and #-comments ignored.
#   2 path    repo-relative path of the thing to load
#   3 when    one line: "always relevant for ..." — the trigger, not a description
#   4 agents  comma list of ba|architect|mdl|gate|test|review, or "all"
#   5 stages  comma list of P,0,1,2,3,4,5,6,7 (conversion-runbook stages), or "-" for none
#   6 tier    baseline     (always-on: goes into every project's CLAUDE.local.md)
#             ondemand     (situational: load when the task calls for it)
#             experimental (under trial: routed and discoverable, but _routing_stage_arm skips
#                          it on purpose, so a skill nobody has proven yet can never be the
#   7 group   which question the skill answers, NOT what kind of thing it is. One of:
#               spine         what am I doing, who decides, how do I ask
#               source        reading a legacy system (migration entry mode only)
#               design        how it looks, before any MDL
#               build         authoring the model — the loop itself
#               build/mdl     the MDL language and tool reference
#               build/agents  Mendix AI agents — the agent document, tools, KBs, chat UI
#               diagnose      something is broken and it may be the tooling
#             The set is CLOSED — routing_validate_groups() rejects anything else, because a
#             typo would otherwise render as a real fourteenth group nobody notices.
#             Added 2026-08-20. Several build/* groups started empty on purpose: a flat list of
#             62 skills hid the fact that this toolkit said nothing at all about workflows,
#             REST, agents, grids or build-time security. The empty group is the finding — and
#             it works: build/workflow, build/integration and build/agents were each filled by
#             a skill written because the empty heading made the hole visible.
#             Groups order the RENDERED tables (ROUTING.md, README's situational table). They
#             deliberately do NOT group the baseline views: baseline is a read-all-of-these set,
#             where sub-headings would imply a selectivity that does not exist, and that view is
#             copied into every project's CLAUDE.local.md — regrouping it churns every project
# TSV rather than a markdown ROUTING.md because a renderer has to parse this in bash 3.2 on
# macOS, and several "when" strings contain the "|" that a markdown table uses as its column
# separator. ROUTING.md at the repo root is the human-readable view — rendered FROM here, so
# it can never disagree with what the scripts install. Kept in bin/lib/ next to
# install-manifest.sh (the same one-manifest-N-readers precedent) and deliberately NOT in
# skills/, which gate-check.sh treats as PROTOCOL_PATHS: a data file there would trip a
# protocol-staleness ack on every routing edit.

column3: when
Any pipeline work at all — every session, before producing any stage artifact (not just "when unsure"); READMEs and the guide are orientation only
Any question before asking the user or writing anything — query the model, then read the source, then ask the human, in that order
Before writing any .js or .sh for a check, gate or report — and before adding a rule to an existing one: judgement goes in a skill, code only fetches facts a reader cannot
Any pass whose input is missing, stale or unresolvable — before recording UNMEASURED, N/A or a silent skip: name what was missing, say what you assessed against instead, still deliver a verdict
Putting a question TO the user — any gate, any stage: ask in chat not in a file, two named options plus your recommendation, one batch per gate then end the turn
Deep, adaptive interview on one topic, on demand, when a checkpoint's 2+1 or a single question batch isn't enough

Any stage transition — the 2+1 format every CAC uses, and the one-register rule (answers land in PROJECT.md, never in a separate state file). The seven CACs themselves are routed per stage in the situational table
CAC-1, closing Stage 0 in EVERY entry mode — scope IN: full scope or a slice, and in what order. Opens with a brainstorm, not options
CAC-1b, after Stage 1 — scope OUT: is what extraction produced what you meant. No gate stops you; run it late against the BRDs if it was skipped
CAC-2, after BRD scaffolding and before enrichment — capability grouping and enrichment order
CAC-3, after BRD validation and before architecture locks — the hidden business rules that are expensive to discover later
CAC-4, after rearchitect sign-off and before any design artifact — branding and UI direction. Opens with a brainstorm
CAC-5, after design sign-off and before the build plan — build order and slice boundaries. Opens with a brainstorm
CAC-6, after Stage 6 passes and before any cutover step — migration mode only, and a hard gate: every answer lands CONFIRMED, no ASSUMED defaults
Setting up or completing a project's dev-process subagents — once, at project start, not "on demand"
Deciding whether to extract at all, before any BRD gets generated
Taking in a new source — before generating anything from it. Grades what the source can support; nothing else in this toolkit reads a source
Rendering a filled triage.md for review — the triage.html surface Stage 0 names. Renders only; the Stage 0 verdict stays with gate-check and the judgement with source-triage.md

Reviewing what the extraction actually produced — the Stage 1 surface, and the file the Stage 1 gate looks for. Renders a code-extracted and a document knowledge base alike, so a requirements-driven project gets the surface too; prints no zero that a second record does not agree with
Deciding who answers a question — before putting any batch to the user. gap/conflict/choice/user-only is what keeps a gate batch at four questions instead of 127
Writing BRDs, especially several in parallel — "build" before the fan-out, "check" before any BRD is called done

Reviewing what the BRDs actually say — the Stage 2 surface, for BRDs from any source. Reads every knowledge base at once, and keeps a section that is absent-because-not-applicable apart from one that is absent-because-expected
Building any module — before the first script. The mdl-agent's single per-module input
Writing ANY MDL script — before the first line. Step 0 picks the write mode, then the STOP table overrides it for corrupting operations

Placing any document in a module — before the first `create`. Feature group, then Pages/Microflows/Services/Resources; the path comes from the brief's folder plan, and the table says which types mxcli can actually place
Writing or fixing any microflow — MDL gotchas plus annotation discipline
Building any page or snippet — before the first widget. Wireframe, tokens, gallery reuse, cross-check; no wireframe means STOP

Writing or reviewing any page or snippet — the spacing scale (8/16/24/32/48), section rhythm, and the page-header scaffold every full page starts with; sections at 0px apart and pages with no H1 are the defects it retires
Building or using the in-app design gallery
Choosing CLI vs MCP+MDL vs hand-rolled MCP, or any MCP write session — three co-equal write modes, not CLI-only

Reviewing any module before calling it done — the ONE pass: build, gate, prove, LOOK (is it logical, does it look right, does it match our design, over every page not just the tested ones), confirm with the denominator stated
Before calling any module tested — what testing a module means, and the false-green register of confirmed ways a test reports green over a broken feature

Finishing any module — before calling it done. One command that runs every instrument and keeps "instrument faulted" apart from "feature failed"; in a wired project run the installed copy at bin/verify-module.sh
A CE error or behavior that looks like a known mxcli quirk rather than a modeling mistake
Generating a new project's CLAUDE.md — baseline routing plus project-specific facts
Auditing or regression/e2e-testing an EXISTING app — no intake, no stages, no gates
Assessing or planning a migration up front, before any pipeline is chosen
Running the extraction pipeline
Migrating from a stack that has no dedicated pipeline
Migrating an OutSystems app
Understanding OutSystems 11 source
Reading the OutSystems XML export schema
Understanding Node/Express+React source, its layout assumptions and its gaps
Scanning or classifying an unstructured document folder
Validating an extractor's output before its BRDs are trusted
Validating a new stack pipeline's extraction quality
Extracting Excel/Word/PDF specs into a knowledge base
Writing or enriching a BRD JSON
Validating BRDs against the code and document KB
Diagramming target architecture — module defs, wiring, fit-gap, marketplace, security, NFRs, integrations
Deciding module boundaries before "create module"
Designing the brand and ONE ANNOTATED WIREFRAME PER SCREEN before building pages — the design system alone is half the deliverable
Turning BRDs plus architecture into a numbered, dependency-ordered build plan
Building the Stage 4 coverage ledger — every requirement either claimed by a build-plan row or catalogued with a reason, never invisible
Checking a coverage ledger against its BRD — every scalar leaf CLAIMED, LEDGERED, UNCLAIMED, PHANTOM or DOUBLE-CLAIMED, so coverage is measured rather than remembered
Building a module with mxcli — verified, iterative, coverage-checklist gated
Writing MDL microflow scripts — worked recipes

Writing a single MDL script that takes a project from nothing to a working vertical slice — execution order, why it is deliberately non-idempotent, the instrument hierarchy, and the silent failures that pass every check
Building and auditing Mendix pages — widget patterns, datasource shapes
Generating a whole page tree in one script — the structure patterns that survive it

Building a Mendix AI agent — the agent is runtime data not a model document, so JSON import, tool microflows, knowledge base chunk loading and the runtime wiring all sit outside MDL, and mxbuild stays green when they are wrong
Embedding a copilot chat panel — the frame is yours, ConversationalUI owns the conversation; wireframe to tokens to snippet to page placement
Running the ledger rung alone — recompute every stored ledger status against the live model and catch the STALE rows that claim built for something the model no longer has
Running the wiring rung alone — a module imported but never reached, an element built but wired to nothing, a boundary crossed; mxbuild and e2e are blind to all three
Before any runtime test — brings the stack up unattended and PROVES the thing that answered is this project's app; --check makes it report-only
Standing up or extending the Playwright e2e harness
Writing DB assertion tests that cross-check UI state against the database

Establishing the data and identities a journey run needs — BEFORE it runs. Derive and measure with project-bin/fixture-manifest.sh first; interview only the residue, and never seed from inside the harness
Proving a module's user journey end-to-end — the deep form of step 3 PROVE; use whenever an instrument reports green and you cannot say what would have made it red
Running the fuzz/crash net on a module whose journeys are already green — and reading the result, which is NOT evidence the module works
UX audit and screenshot-loop discipline
Tracking scope delta between the BRD and the built state
Cutover and retrospective — promoting proven patterns back into the toolkit
Writing or reading docs/report.json — the append-only contract every instrument writes to and every renderer reads; open BEFORE building a new instrument or a second renderer
Installing, extending, debugging or porting the verification harness — which part owns what, which parts run standalone, and what a missing part must report
Before citing ANY behavioural claim about the harness, the Mendix runtime or a test tool as evidence — a claim not in the register may not be cited
Any time an exit code, a tool's output or a subagent's report is about to become a stated finding — verify before you conclude
Checking whether the whole journey hangs together rather than each piece — finds correctly-built components nothing reaches, which per-element conformance and UI tests both miss
After every module's CONFIRM stage — counts proven modules since the last cluster/full coherence pass and exits DUE once the threshold is reached, so the cadence isn't left to memory

After marking a module done, or any time "how much is built vs proven" is asked — renders build-plan.html from done- prefixes and verify-module.sh/improvement-register.md, kept as two honestly separate views
Turning an already-rigorous run into a narrated proof a stakeholder can trust without running anything
Studio Pro will not load the project, or the .mpr looks gutted — recover before relaunching SP, never git checkout
Running lint as a gate rather than a report — per-rule ratchet against a committed baseline, plus the crash and collapse guards that stop a blind rule passing
Reading a lint result, or writing/repairing any .star rule — lint's failure mode is a confident clean pass, so 0 findings is a claim needing evidence
Any review pass that runs more than once — module-review, coherence, monkey, wiring-sweep: findings accumulate across runs, a per-run report cannot show a trend
Writing an actual .journey.json — the worked field-by-field reference for the contract journey-proof.md argues for
Every module before it is called done — does every clickable thing actually do something; run AFTER the happy-path journey is green, never before

Writing or debugging a Mendix native Workflow (CREATE WORKFLOW/USER TASK/OUTCOMES) — syntax, the 11 workflow microflow statements, DECISION vs CALL MICROFLOW, and the two corruption classes (binary-version $Type, and create-before-reference)
Building a REST integration (consumed or published) for the first time on a project — the checks that avoid a rebuild after the first live call
Working with the Mendix Epics board programmatically — creating/reading stories and epics, updating workflow state, or integrating BRDs with the portal
Preparing an mxcli/Studio Pro bug for submission — scope pinning, read-back-vs-write-path verification, gate-sensitivity negative controls, severity scoping, before it's called filable
A page/grid/combobox renders empty (blank cells, zero rows, zero options) during UI review or an e2e run — before assuming a single cause
Suspecting an mxcli/mxbuild tool defect and deciding whether to swap a binary — proving it's version-specific without risking the real model
Restarting Studio Pro on macOS — the reopen bug, the port bug, and detecting a real hang vs a slow load
Building or auditing a collapsible sidebar nav — Atlas Core's collapsed state needs icons assigned per menu item or it silently clips label text
Writing a popup page's microflow with a retry/validation-failure branch that re-shows the same popup — missing close page stacks duplicate dialogs
Writing MDL for a datagrid column with ShowContentAs customContent that needs to display a bound value
Writing a popup whose primary button creates/commits an object or triggers a backend flow — MDL has no native toast, so feedback must be explicit
Extracting structured requirements from a large delivered document corpus into per-scope knowledge-base files
Turning a client-derived Mendix app into a clean, shareable demo with zero client fingerprint — branding, data, custom widgets
Driving the whole toolkit pipeline on a real source to find what the written skills don't say — the toolkit is the subject, not the app it builds
